summary: A strong chapter already; add misconception-mapped MCQ distractors and a clarification on reading mixtures of halide ions, since several past papers (and 'extra' items x005/x013/x016) test exactly that and the note only walks through a single halide at a time.

improvements.why: no generated item maps a distractor to a misconception (m3/m4); past papers (e.g. 9701_s21_13_q16, 9701_s20_11_q12) test a mixture of two halides, which the note and worked example never cover for a single halide
improvements.what: MCQ: a mixture of sodium chloride and sodium bromide is treated with excess silver nitrate then excess concentrated ammonia; which precipitate remains? Correct answer AgBr (cream); distractors: 'no precipitate' mapped to m3 (all silver halides dissolve in dilute ammonia), 'a white precipitate (AgCl)' mapped to m4-style colour confusion, 'a yellow precipitate (AgI)' as an identity-confusion distractor not present in this mixture

improvements.why: no generated item maps a distractor to m2 (concentrated sulfuric acid oxidises chloride)
improvements.what: MCQ: concentrated sulfuric acid is added separately to solid sodium chloride and solid sodium iodide; which correctly compares the sulfur-containing products? Correct answer identifies only NaI gives reduced sulfur species; a distractor stating chlorine gas forms from NaCl mapped to m2, and a distractor reversing the reducing-strength order mapped to m1

improvements.why: several past MCQs (9701_w21_13_q16, 9701_s20_11_q12, 9701_w20_11_q23-style mixtures) test a mixture of two halide ions rather than one, and the note's method and worked example only walk through a single halide
improvements.what: A short paragraph or bullet on reading a mixture of halide ions: excess silver nitrate precipitates all halides present; the precipitate's overall colour can be misleading, so judge composition by what partly dissolves in dilute ammonia (any AgCl present), what then dissolves in concentrated ammonia (any AgBr present), and what residue remains (AgI, if present)
